sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Beyond the previous precise points, we must understand why the acceptance of the Jews occurred specifically during the decree of Haman, when they had actual self-sacrifice, even though the Torah was already given with "we will do and we will hear" and the command of Kriyas Shema.

translations.translation: Now, in addition to the precise points above,
we must also understand the content of the explanation
(in the maamar)
that this "and the Jews accepted" was at the time of the decree because then they had mesirus nefesh for Torah and mitzvos,
for seemingly,
regarding the vast majority of mitzvos it is written,
"which a man shall do and live by them,"
and even regarding the three mitzvos about which it is said "be killed and do not transgress,"
they are not a matter of mesirus nefesh, but rather that the manner of their fulfillment is even if one is killed because of it,
and the mitzvah of mesirus nefesh for sanctification of G-d's Name is only one mitzvah,
so what was the necessity for mesirus nefesh for the acceptance
(and the Jews accepted)
of the entire Torah?
And what is said in Tanya,
that the reason Moshe Rabbeinu commanded the generation that entered the Land to recite Kriyas Shema twice daily to accept upon themselves the yoke of the kingdom of heaven with mesirus nefesh
(even though He promised them "your fear and dread shall G-d place" etc.)
is because the fulfillment of the Torah and its mitzvos depends on this, that one always remember the matter of his self-sacrifice to G-d,
the matter of mesirus nefesh upon which the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos depends is mesirus nefesh in potential
(that if he would need to give his life for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos, he is prepared for this)
and not actual mesirus nefesh,
and yet at the giving of the Torah,
when they said "we will do and we will hear"
(and certainly after they were commanded to recite Kriyas Shema twice daily)
they accepted upon themselves to fulfill whatever they would be commanded, even if it would require mesirus nefesh for this,
and nevertheless,
there was not a complete acceptance
(and the Jews accepted)
until the time of Haman's decree,
when they had actual mesirus nefesh.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: There were two times of actual mesirus nefesh for Torah and mitzvos—Chanukah and Purim—and the acceptance of the Jews was specifically through the mesirus nefesh of Purim, which is more connected to the completion of receiving the Torah.

translations.translation: Now, it is known that at two times there was actual mesirus nefesh
[of all of Israel]
for Torah and mitzvos,
at Chanukah
(at the time of the Greek decree)
and at Purim
(at the time of Haman's decree).
And since all matters in the Torah are with utmost precision,
it must be said,
that this matter of "and the Jews accepted" was specifically through the mesirus nefesh of Purim,
it is
(not only because the mesirus nefesh of Purim preceded the mesirus nefesh of Chanukah,
but also)
because the mesirus nefesh of Purim is more connected to
(the completion of)
receiving the Torah.
And we must understand the difference between the mesirus nefesh of Chanukah and the mesirus nefesh of Purim,
that because of this difference,
the completion of receiving the Torah is specifically through the mesirus nefesh of Purim.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The innovation of the Giving of the Torah was that it united the spiritual and physical in mitzvos, enabling the physical object to become a vessel for holiness through the revelation of Ein Sof, which transcends both, and this corresponds to three levels in fulfilling mitzvos: from the animal soul, from the G-dly soul, and with self-nullification.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing
the known
that the innovation of the Giving of the Torah regarding the Torah and mitzvos that existed before the Giving of the Torah,
is that the mitzvos of the Patriarchs
(and in general—before the Giving of the Torah)
were only in spirituality.
For in addition to the fact that many mitzvos were fulfilled only spiritually
(like tefillin, which mention the Exodus from Egypt, and at that time the Egyptian exile had not yet occurred),
even regarding the mitzvos they fulfilled in physicality,
the drawing down of holiness was only in spirituality and not in the physical object with which they fulfilled the mitzvah.
For before the Giving of the Torah, there was the decree that "the upper ones shall not descend to the lower, and the lower ones shall not ascend to the upper,"
and therefore there was no connection of the holiness of the mitzvah
(upper ones)
with the physical object with which the mitzvah is performed
(lower ones),
unlike the fulfillment of mitzvos
after the Giving of the Torah,
when the decree and partition between the upper and lower was nullified,
the connection was made of the physical object
(with which the mitzvah is performed)
with the holiness of the mitzvah,
to the extent that in several mitzvos,
the physical object becomes the object of the mitzvah.
And based on the known
that the connection of two opposite things is through a matter that transcends both of them,
it is understood,

that the connection of upper and lower that occurred at the Giving of the Torah is through the fact that at the Giving of the Torah there was a drawing down of the Ein Sof light that is beyond the category of above and below
(upper and lower).
And from all this it is understood,
that in the mitzvos after the Giving of the Torah,
there are three matters.
The lower
[for even after the Giving of the Torah,
that the physical object with which the mitzvah is performed becomes the object of the mitzvah,
it is not transformed into spirituality and remains a physical object],
the upper
[for even after the Giving of the Torah,
when the holiness of the mitzvah is drawn down and fixed in the physical object,
it is a spiritual matter],
and the nullification of the categories of upper and lower,
that this that the upper and lower connect with each other
(despite being opposites)
is through the nullification of their category,
which is brought about by the drawing down of the Ein Sof light that transcends both of them.
And it can be said,
that these three matters have their parallel also in the fulfillment of mitzvos.
When a person fulfills the mitzvos in the manner of "a mitzvah of men, learned,"
that is, out of habit that he has become accustomed to,
since habit becomes nature,
his fulfillment of mitzvos is from the side of the nature of the body and the animal soul,
the lower in man,
and when he fulfills the mitzvos because he loves G-d and desires to cleave to Him, and it is impossible to truly cleave to Him except through fulfilling the 248 positive commandments, which are
the 248 limbs of the King,
his fulfillment of mitzvos is from the side of the soul
(the G-dly soul),
the upper in man.
And when he fulfills the mitzvos for their own sake,
not because of the benefit that will come to him through this
(nor even spiritual benefit)
but because the mitzvos are the will of the Blessed One,
his fulfillment of mitzvos is not from the side of his own existence
(nor even the existence of the soul)
but in self-nullification,
that his entire being
(at the time he fulfills the mitzvah)
is only to fulfill the will of the Supreme One.
